es: Reconocer it is said that, it is believed that y there is thought to be para separar rumores, creencias generales y hechos comprobados.

teaching.en: It is said that there is treasure under the old bridge.
teaching.es: Se dice que hay un tesoro bajo el puente viejo.
teaching.explanationEs: It is said that + oración: un rumor que circula, sin decir quién lo cuenta.
segments: It is said that there is
teaching.audioText: It is said that there is treasure under the old bridge.

teaching.en: It is believed that the mayor will leave the town next year.
teaching.es: Se cree que el alcalde dejará la ciudad el año que viene.
teaching.explanationEs: It is believed that: lo que mucha gente piensa, sin pruebas firmes.
segments: It is believed that the mayor
will leave the town next year.
teaching.audioText: It is believed that the mayor will leave the town next year.

teaching.en: There is thought to be a tunnel under the old hotel.
teaching.es: Se piensa que hay un túnel bajo el viejo hotel.
teaching.explanationEs: There is thought to be + algo: presenta como creencia que algo existe.
segments: There is thought to be a
teaching.audioText: There is thought to be a tunnel under the old hotel.

teaching.en: It has been confirmed that the bridge will close on Monday.
teaching.es: Se ha confirmado que el puente cerrará el lunes.
teaching.explanationEs: It has been confirmed that: hecho comprobado, con una fuente fiable.
segments: It has been confirmed that the
teaching.audioText: It has been confirmed that the bridge will close on Monday.

teaching.en: There is no proof that the old hotel is haunted.
teaching.es: No hay pruebas de que el viejo hotel esté embrujado.
teaching.explanationEs: Si no hay proof, el rumor sigue siendo solo un rumor.
teaching.audioText: There is no proof that the old hotel is haunted.

teaching.en: The newspaper printed the rumour last week, but nobody knows where it started.
teaching.es: El periódico publicó el rumor la semana pasada, pero nadie sabe dónde empezó.
teaching.explanationEs: Un rumor puede llegar al periódico y seguir sin una fuente clara: por eso se usa la forma impersonal.
segments: The newspaper printed the rumour last week,
but nobody knows where it started.
teaching.audioText: The newspaper printed the rumour last week, but nobody knows where it started.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta un rumor sin decir quién lo cuenta?

choices.text: It has been confirmed that the old hotel is closed.
It is said that the old hotel is haunted.
The mayor says that the old hotel is empty.

feedback.es: It is said that presenta lo que circula entre la gente, sin fuente ni prueba; las otras dos citan a una persona o dan un hecho confirmado.

hint.es: Busca la estructura que equivale a «se dice que».

origin.text: Quieres contar lo que repite la gente: el viejo hotel está embrujado. Nadie lo ha comprobado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se cree que el alcalde es muy rico.»

feedback.es: «Se cree» es it is believed (o thought) that: el participio de un verbo de opinión va después de is.

hint.es: Es una creencia general: necesitas el participio de un verbo de opinión.

origin.text: It is ___ that the mayor is very rich.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase habla de un hecho y no de un rumor?

choices.text: It is said that the library will open on Friday.
It is believed that the library will open on Friday.
It has been confirmed that the library will open on Friday.

feedback.es: Solo it has been confirmed indica una fuente comprobada; said y believed dejan la noticia en rumor o en creencia.
